reviews.comment: Beautiful morning light along the shophouses. I loved finding the little tiled entrances between the souvenir stalls.
The walk between the old shopfronts was pleasant, and the painted shutters made for some nice photos.
The old five-foot ways are wonderful. I enjoyed taking my time over the door carvings near the temple.
The shop signs were interesting but the bicycles made the narrow lane crowded. Okay for one quick loop.
The lanterns and shaded verandahs were cantik. A nice stretch to walk before the shops open.
The main photo corner was too crowded. Frustrating to keep stepping around people posing beside the wall.
The textures around the old clan house were amazing. This was my favourite place for a slow photo walk.
Breathtaking view over the island when the clouds lifted. The early funicular ride was wonderful.
The upper paths were peaceful once I walked past the station. Lovely shade under the bigger trees.
We loved watching the city wake up from the railing. The cooler air was excellent after town.
Cantik lah, especially the layers of hills looking towards the mainland. I would visit again for the morning light.
The funicular climb itself was interesting. The walk round the top was relaxing with plenty of spots to pause.
The ride queue was frustrating and the viewing deck too crowded. I could barely get to the railing.
The cool breeze was nice, but the queues by the lift were tiring. Biasa for me overall.
The trees around the upper track were beautiful. It felt peaceful even though George Town was just below us.
The temple roofs looked beautiful from the lower staircase, and the bronze statue was impressive up close.
I enjoyed following the courtyard levels. The little painted details on the roof were lovely.
The lanterns by the passage were cantik. An amazing view opens out when you reach the higher courtyard.
The route through the souvenir passage was confusing. The long waiting time at the incline lift was frustrating.
The carvings were beautiful but getting from one level to the next was tiring. A mixed afternoon for me.
Nice to see the pagoda between the rooftops as we climbed. The upper courtyard felt peaceful.
We enjoyed the wooden walk and the friendly stalls near the entrance. The little boats made nice photos.
The view between the houses was lovely, but the walkway got crowded whenever people stopped for pictures.
The planks were difficult to navigate in the crush. I found the narrow stretch near the end frustrating.
The water looked beautiful from the end of the jetty. I loved seeing the houses on stilts in that light.
The char koay teow was sedap and the smoky wok smell had me queuing again. Great supper with friends.
Good assam laksa and a friendly stallholder who explained the toppings. We enjoyed sharing small portions.
Our oyster omelette was overpriced and the food court got noisy. The long queues made supper frustrating.
The satay was tasty enough and the table was okay. It was an ordinary supper for our group.
The hawker stalls were interesting to browse. Our rojak was delicious, especially the tangy sauce.
Beautiful sunset near the sand, with the fishing boats silhouetted. I loved sitting there after the heat eased.
A relaxing walk where the beach curves away from the busier stretch. The evening breeze was pleasant.
The sand where we sat was dirty and the jet ski noise was awful. I would not return for a swim.
The horizon was beautiful, but the busy water-sports area was noisy. Okay for a quick walk.
Cantik evening sky over the water. The softer sand further along made for a lovely stroll.
I found the line of water-sports booths unpleasant. The area was too crowded for the quiet beach break I wanted.
The bicycle mural looked wonderful against the worn plaster. I loved the way people lined up to take turns.
I enjoyed spotting the wire figures between the murals. It was a nice way to look up from the map.
Some pieces were interesting, but the lanes were crowded around the main stops. An okay walk overall.
Tracking down the faded murals was confusing and disappointing. The busiest corners took ages to get through.
The wall colours were amazing in the late light. Finding the smaller paintings away from the queue was seronok.
The carved furniture and beadwork were amazing. I loved the little details in the tiled courtyard.
The guide's explanation of the wedding clothes was interesting. The old dining room was impressive.
The jewellery displays were beautiful, but the upstairs landing was crowded. A mixed visit for me.
I enjoyed looking at the old household objects in the cabinets. The upstairs rooms were surprisingly lovely.
The giant trees were beautiful and the lower path felt peaceful in the early morning. I would come again.
Bagus for a slow walk. The shady route near the stream was relaxing and the garden signs were helpful.
The signposts were confusing near the paths I wanted. The detour in the midday heat was tiring.
The bamboo walkway was beautiful and I loved smelling the crushed leaves at the spice display.
The labelled ginger plants were menarik. It was a worthwhile walk under the trees even in the heat.
The spice signs were interesting but the uneven steps were tiring. Okay if you take it slowly.
The slippery path felt uncomfortable and the route signs were poor. For me it was a disappointing outing.
The butterfly garden was amazing. I loved waiting by the flowers until the blue wings opened.
The displays about pupae were interesting, and the garden paths were pleasant to wander with the kids.
Seronok seeing butterflies land beside the waterfall. The indoor exhibits were excellent too.
The butterflies were beautiful but the indoor corridor got crowded. The visit felt mixed.
I enjoyed spotting different wings at the feeding stations. The staff member by the exhibit was helpful.
The giant cendol display was great fun, and I enjoyed reading the labels about local dishes.
Some of the food models were interesting but the last room felt ordinary. Okay for a short visit.
I found the photo displays boring after a while. The tight space was uncomfortable once more visitors came in.
The long queues were terrible. The crowded platform felt awful and I would not return.
I loved the beautiful wooden houses and the wonderful view over the water.
The sand by our spot was dirty, and the jet ski noise made the afternoon unpleasant.
The lanterns were beautiful and the view over the roofs was amazing. I would come again.
The exhibits were boring. The tight photo corners were awful and the visit was a waste of time.
The butterfly garden was fantastic, the waterfall was beautiful, and the displays were excellent.
There were two rooms before the staircase and some objects behind glass.
We reached around eight and ordered at the third stall near the end.
